newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks open higher as bullion boosts golds.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks open higher as bullion boosts golds.

text.p: CHANGE CHANGE
NIKKEI 20157.02 -92.30 LME CASH NICKEL US$6715 +5.0
CANDLR 1.3786 LME CASH ALUM US$1579.0 +25.0
CAN 30-YR 119.02 +0.36 BRENT CRUDE US$18.16 +0.07
* Toronto stocks opened higher in quiet trade as gold issues climbed more than one percent on stronger COMEX prices. * All but one sub-index gained ground. * 14.1 million shares traded.
Toronto stocks opened higher on Tuesday as rising bullion prices boosted gold issues more than one percent in light early trade and most other sectors recouped some of yesterday's losses.
Traders said the market was a bit stronger than expected ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, which begins at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT.

"The market seems to be getting back on track ahead of the Humphrey-Hawkins testimony and people seem to have settled down a bit," said Fred Ketchen, senior vice-president and director of equity trading at ScotiaMcLeod Inc.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index rose 27.23 points to 6674.62 in turnover of 14.1 million shares worth C$199.7 million. Advances outpaced declines 263 to 218, while 230 issues traded unchanged.
Golds led 13 sectors higher, gaining 137.67 points or 1.63 percent as COMEX August gold rose US$2.60 an ounce in early New York trade.
Ketchen said traders will be keeping their eye on Greenspan's testimony to U.S. Congress but noted that no explosive news is expected.

"I think that the general feeling now with respect to what he's going to say is that we don't have any inflation and the Fed doesn't have to do anything now but they're going to have to keep vigilant," Ketchen said.
--- HOT STOCKS ---

* Shares in Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce were up 0.35 to 38.25 in moderate trade after the bank said its wholly-owned brokerage arm, CIBC-Wood Gundy Inc, has made a deal to buy privately owned New York brokerage Oppenheimer & Co for US$525 million. The deal was widely anticipated.

* Shares in Barrick Gold Corp were up 0.85 to 31.30 in healthy trade after the gold producer said it expects to report higher year-over-year earnings and cash flow for 1997 despite the lower second-quarter profits reported today.

* Shares in Potash Corp of Saskatchewan fell 5.90 to 102.10 in light trade after the German government disallowed the sale of German chemical giant BASF AG 's Kali & Salz unit to Potash Corp. Potash Corp said it will "thoroughly review" its position on the purchase and respects Bonn's decision.

* Spar Aerospace said today it will contest a lawsuit filed by numerous companies claiming damages related to an alleged irregularity in the performance of Spar's MSAT satellite. Spar shares were down 1.20 to 10.55 in thin trade.
